Year 7 Science · Unit plan

Unit: Forces & Motion

6 weeks · 18 lessons (3 a week), 2 of them optional · Victorian Curriculum F–10 v2.0

Students build a working model of force as a push or a pull, apply Newton’s three laws to everyday motion, then use energy transfer and the law of the lever to explain simple machines and a trebuchet’s throw. Five experiments build toward an open, class-shared investigation of how trebuchet range and arm spin change with counterweight mass, assessed by an open-booklet Investigation Test in Lesson 18.

Achievement standard · Levels 7–8

  • Science Understanding. Explain how balanced and unbalanced forces, including gravity, change an object’s motion, represented with force diagrams; calculate the mechanical advantage of simple machines; analyse energy transfers and transformations for efficiency.
  • Science Inquiry. Develop hypotheses and reasoned predictions; plan reproducible, safe and ethical investigations and select equipment that records data precisely; organise data in tables and graphs; analyse patterns, trends and anomalies; identify assumptions and sources of error; support conclusions with evidence and communicate findings for a purpose. The trebuchet investigation and test carry almost this whole strand.
  • Science as a Human Endeavour. Explain how new evidence can lead to changes in scientific knowledge (Lesson 12’s reading on Galileo).

Content descriptors

VC2S8U14
Balanced and unbalanced forces acting on objects, including gravitational force, represented with force diagrams; changes in motion relate to mass and force
VC2S8U13
Simple machines, including the lever, change the direction and size of forces
VC2S8U15
Energy exists in different forms, including gravitational and elastic; energy transfers and transformations, and their efficiency
VC2S8H01
Scientific knowledge, including models and theories, can change in light of new evidence
VC2S8I01–I08
Science inquiry — questioning and predicting (I01); planning and conducting (I02–I03); processing, modelling and analysing (I04–I05); evaluating (I06–I07); communicating (I08)
VC2S10U17
Levels 9–10, above level — Newton’s laws of motion and the equations of motion
VC2S10U15
Levels 9–10, above level — conservation of energy in energy transfers and transformations

Prepare for learning

  • Lesson 1’s opening quiz checks primary-school ideas about push/pull forces before anything new is taught.
  • Every later deck opens with a five-question review: three on the lesson before, two from older lessons.

Review and reflect

  • The opening review quiz in every deck; Part C checked in class each lesson; an exit question closing each lesson.
  • Task 12’s odd-result discussion and the booklet-completion check in Lesson 17, ahead of the test.

Modifications for DI and IEPs

  • Reading and comprehension come before any calculation; worked examples are revealed one step at a time.
  • Sentence starters, word banks and a worked first row in red on every write-in table.
  • Experiment 4 and the lever lessons use masses and arm lengths only (no newtons) until Lesson 9 introduces force units for MA.

Extension

  • Part D of every lesson, several flagged above level (VC2S10U17, VC2S10U15).
  • Optional Year 8 Lessons 11 and 14; Section C of the Trebuchet Investigation Test.

Print the whole thing

  • Whole Lesson Booklet (Lessons 1–14, 158 pp.)
  • Trebuchet Investigation booklet (Lessons 15–18)
  • Trebuchet Investigation — condensed booklet

Each lesson row links its own booklet pages for printing one section at a time.

  • Every lesson has its own slide deck and its own booklet section in four parts: A Reading · B Theory and examples · C Practice · D Above level. Lessons 15–18 run from the Trebuchet Investigation booklet.
  • Lessons 11 and 14 are optional Year 8 extensions; skip both and the unit runs in 16 lessons.
  • Above level: Newton’s laws by name and the equations of motion are Levels 9–10 (VC2S10U17); conservation of energy as a law is Levels 9–10 (VC2S10U15). Lessons 4–8 and 12–13 use them as tools for the experiments, not as Year 7 standards.
